title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Rate Class for Detention Days and Non-Operating Reefers
content:
## Clause

For detention billed on a Demurrage and Detention Free Time record, the rate class of the container is the one the equipment class map gives it, with one exception that depends on the booking the container travels under. Whether a reefer-mapped unit keeps reefer-class rates turns on that booking: only a booking whose cargo is reefer keeps it there. With cargo of any other type on the booking the unit is treated as a non-operating reefer, whose days are all charged at the dry-class rate.

Each detention day is then priced at the detention rate that the product on the record sets for that day's slab and for the rate class so determined.

## Truth table

| Class in the equipment class map | Cargo type of the booking | Class used for detention pricing |
|---|---|---|
| dry | any | dry |
| special | any | special |
| reefer | reefer | reefer |
| reefer | anything other than reefer | dry |

## Points of judgement

- The cargo type is read from the booking under which the container moves, which is the booking the free-time record belongs to.
- The exception only ever moves a reefer unit into the dry class; it never alters a dry or special unit.
- Which product's rates apply is decided by the product on the record, and the slab of each day by its position in the detention slab count.

**Q: How are the detention days of a non-operating reefer priced?**
The dry-class detention scale of the product on the record, because a reefer unit under a booking whose cargo type is not reefer is a non-operating reefer.
